title: COCO: DINOv3 ViT-B/16 cells, object and background annotations

about.summary: Each point is one 32 × 32 px cell (7 × 7 grid) of a COCO photo, embedded by DINOv3 ViT-B/16 (self-supervised (DINOv3, LVD-1689M)) and projected with UMAP. 20,580 cells from 420 images: 30 per class for 14 classes chosen in groups that share a kind of background. The same images and cells are shown for all models in this series.

sections.title: Source
items: COCO 2017 training images (Lin et al. 2014) with instance masks for 80 object classes, and COCO-Stuff (Caesar et al. 2018) pixel maps for 91 background classes.
Classes, grouped by shared background: savanna (zebra, giraffe, elephant), pasture (horse, cow, sheep), sky (airplane, bird), indoors (cat, dog), street (car, bus, motorcycle, bicycle).
Per class, 30 images drawn at random (seed 0) among images where the class covers the largest annotated area, no person is annotated, and the class is the majority label of at least 2 cells.
Images are loaded from Flickr, where COCO collected them, under their owners' licences. Images no longer on Flickr, or whose Flickr copy differs from the COCO file, were skipped.

sections.title: Processing
items: Centre square crop resized to 224 × 224 px, normalized as the model expects.

DINOv3 ViT-B/16 (timm vit_base_patch16_dinov3.lvd1689m), self-supervised (DINOv3, LVD-1689M); features: patch tokens after the final norm, averaged 2 × 2 (14 × 14 tokens), giving the same 7 × 7 cells for every model in this series.
UMAP with cosine distance, 30 neighbours, min_dist 0.1, random_state 0.

sections.title: Colour options (COCO ground truth only)
items: Pixel labels are painted from the annotations, background classes first, then objects from the largest to the smallest; each cell takes the label of most of its pixels.
region: object (one of the 80 classes), background (one of the 91 stuff classes) or unlabelled.
category / supercategory: the cell's class and its COCO supercategory.
image_label: the class the image was chosen for (its largest annotated category), repeated for all 49 cells, as a dataset with one label per image would give it.

sections.title: Caveats
items: Background groups (savanna, pasture, ...) describe how classes were chosen; they are not annotations.
A 32 px cell can cover parts of several objects; the colour shows only the majority label.
Bicycles and cars are often small or see-through, so many of their images have few object cells.
UMAP distorts global distances; nearby points are similar, far-apart clusters are not necessarily dissimilar.
